::: {.laser-introduction}
## Introduction

Quality assurance of co-registration in XY and Z verifies whether multiple fluorescence channels are spatially aligned as expected. Even small chromatic shifts can distort overlay images, misrepresent co-localization, and compromise quantitative distance measurements.

Routine monitoring with multicolor reference samples helps detect alignment drift and supports spatially accurate, reproducible imaging.
:::

## What is assessed

### X, Y, and Z registration

The signed X, Y, and Z positions of the same reference objects are compared across fluorescence channels. Separate component plots preserve the direction of displacement along every axis.

### Three-dimensional displacement

The Euclidean distance combines all three components as √(X² + Y² + Z²), showing the total displacement from the designated reference channel.

::: {.qa-method-note}
#### Reading the chromatic-aberration dashboards

Shift vectors are displayed in nanometers relative to the 488 nm reference channel. X, Y, and Z are shown as separate signed plots, and the 3D-distance plot shows their Euclidean magnitude. Use each objective dashboard to compare channels and follow registration over time.
:::
